plan_a_advantages: Potentially less taxing on the body due to the consistent easy runs
plan_b_advantages: Incorporates hill and threshold training for speed development
More targeted workouts to improve climbing strength and endurance
Greater variety in workout types to prevent boredom and promote adaptation
reasoning: Plan B is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates more targeted workouts designed to build specific trail running skills like climbing strength and threshold endurance, which are crucial for faster times. Plan A, conversely, focuses almost entirely on easy runs, which while beneficial for recovery, won't directly translate to improved speed. Plan B’s inclusion of hill workouts and a dedicated threshold session provides a more effective stimulus for increasing running power and efficiency, key components of trail speed.  Plan A’s repetitive easy runs risk leading to plateaus, whereas Plan B’s varied workouts will challenge the athlete in a more progressive way.
